conflicts.description: The Council wants to keep any vault seed stock under arcology control, while the Seedkeepers insist it belong to all, so the heroes' mission risks becoming a political fight.
conflicts.name: Who Owns the Seeds

conflicts.description: The Array Wardens want to spend scarce resources to reclaim the satellite, while the Council wants to save them for evacuation and rationing.
conflicts.name: Reclaim or Ration

conflicts.description: The Dustwalkers charge high tolls for safe passage, and they are suspicious of arcology folk who offer little in return.
conflicts.name: The Price of the Crossing

description: In a near-future Earth ravaged by climate collapse, humanity survives inside a network of solar-powered arcologies called Greenholds. Their terraced gardens, mirrored light-towers and living walls are fed by the sun and tended by generations who remember the old world only through stories. Beyond the arcology gates lie the toxic Wastes: salt flats, acid dust seas and the skeletons of drowned cities. This is a post-apocalyptic solarpunk world with a hopeful tone. Cooperation, ingenuity and care for living things are the tools of survival. The western arcology, Greenhold Westreach, is threatened by Helios Wake, a rogue weather satellite that has begun focusing concentrated sunlight onto the ground. A solar storm is also approaching, and it will cripple the arcology's grid and scorch its crops. A young engineer and a reclusive botanist must cross the Wastes to reach the forgotten Deepseed Vault. It holds heat-tolerant seed stock that could let the Greenholds adapt, and it may also hold the old codes needed to reclaim the satellite. The journey tests trust between generations and between disciplines, and it tests whether the Greenholds can choose to share what they have.

factions.description: The cautious governing body of Greenhold Westreach. It rations power and food, and it distrusts anyone who leaves the arcology.
factions.name: Westreach Council

factions.description: Engineers who maintain the Sunspire Array. They believe the satellite can be reclaimed and resent the Council's hoarding of spare parts.
factions.name: Array Wardens

factions.description: Nomadic traders and guides who know the safe routes through the Wastes. They trade in filters and guidance, and they trade in seeds when they can find them.
factions.name: The Dustwalkers

factions.description: A scattered order of botanists who believe seeds belong to everyone. They guard the legend and the location of the Deepseed Vault.
factions.name: The Seedkeepers

history.description: Climate collapse drowned coasts and scorched farmland, ending the old nations.
history.name: The Great Heat

history.description: Botanists sealed the Deepseed Vault as the last copy of the world's seeds, and its location was recorded only in Seedkeeper lore.
history.name: The Vault Sealed

history.description: Survivors built Westreach with sunlight-fed terraces, founding the arcology network.
history.name: The First Greenhold Rises

history.description: Engineers finished the Sunspire Array and its uplink to the weather satellites that stabilized local climate.
history.name: Sunspire Array Completed

history.description: A cascading fault in the weather satellite began focusing sunlight onto Westreach's outer fields, and the first crops burned.
history.name: Helios Wake Goes Rogue

locations.description: A tiered solar arcology of glass terraces, photovoltaic canopies and vertical farms. It is the home of the young engineer and the first target of Helios Wake's burning beam.
locations.name: Greenhold Westreach

locations.description: A towering ring of mirrors and photovoltaic fields on the ridge above Westreach. It supplies the arcology's solar power, and its control hall holds the only uplink to the rogue satellite.
locations.name: The Sunspire Array

locations.description: A toxic expanse of fused sand, acid dust storms and sun-bleached ruins. Its glittering drifts cut skin and clog filters, and travelers cross it only in sealed solar-powered crawlers.
locations.name: The Glasswind Wastes

locations.description: A nomad trading post built from salvaged freight cars and sail-shaded awnings in the middle of the Wastes. Traders barter filters, seeds and repairs here, and it is the only safe stop on the crossing.
locations.name: Rustmarket Halt

locations.description: A forgotten seed bank buried in a cold mountain. Its sealed halls hold pre-collapse seed stock and archived records, and a dormant solar-fed power core keeps them alive.
locations.name: The Deepseed Vault

name: The Verdant Remnant

rules.statement: All sustained power in the Greenholds comes from solar collection; every machine, crawler and light must be built around stored sunlight.
Chemical explosives and firearms are unknown; the Greenholds use pressure tools, mirrors and mechanical devices for cutting, defense and construction.
Exposure to Glasswind dust without a sealed filter causes lung damage within hours, and storms make crossing impossible.
A major solar storm disables unshielded electronics and heats the surface; shielded vaults and deep structures survive it.
Helios Wake can focus sunlight only when it has clear sky and a charged reflector, so its beam weakens at night and under heavy cloud.
By Greenhold custom, no seed stock may be sold, owned or withheld in times of famine; breaking this custom is the gravest social offense.
